pairs.subject: bounded-enumeration
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:101 Runs materializes the entire kernel job collection before slicing it to 500 rows, so the display cap does not bound server memory as job history grows.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:99 The kernel listing accepts neither a position nor a limit; its implementation reads and parses every matching job before Runs slices the result.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx:101 Runs refreshes its rendered window when events arrive; it does not expose a multi-page collection walk whose cross-page consistency must be documented.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:85 The loader supplies a fixed internal ceiling; this context does not merge listing policies or expose recursive enumeration.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/readKeys.ts:13 readKeys selects keyboard bindings, not resource permissions; the inspected listing paths do not hide individual jobs according to caller access.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:37 The fixed ceiling has no documented memory target, worst-case entry size, overhead calculation, deploy-time override, or stated screen-size rationale.
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts:70 This server-render loader accepts only a clock argument; it does not introduce or parse a client-supplied limit parameter.
